brief:
Tomorrow, 14 October, is Legs A, not Legs B. Legs A was due on 10 October and was not trained (you wrote "Sick today" on 8 October and nothing was logged until 12 October), and the last direct quad work was 28 September, so the app sends you to Legs A first. First time on these machines at Chennai, so every number is a starting point to find the weight, not a raise: leg press, feet low, 150, 170, 190 for 8 to 10 (your Warsaw feet-low numbers from 28 September, which were also Singapore's feet-high numbers on 5 October; if 150 is easy go 170, 190, 210); Bulgarian split squat 20 lb dumbbells (9 or 10 kg) for 8 on both sets, up from 17.5 because dumbbells are the same in any gym; leg curl 120 for 12 on all three; leg extension 130 for 12, a guess for this machine, log what you use; adductor 80 then 90 and abductor 60 then 70, the second number only if the first set was easy at 15; calf press 270 to find it, then 290 for 12 twice (Singapore's first two sets); cable crunch 55 for 12, then 60 for 10 twice if it was easy.

This is the automatic review, re-reading everything through tonight's Pull B (18 of 20 sets at Chennai; face pulls skipped). Nothing new has been logged since the review written earlier today, so the program stays at version 2: Push A has a lateral raise after the shoulder press in place of the rope pushdown (side delts were getting 4 sets a week, triceps 14 direct sets); Push B is 3 sets of dips and 3 of lateral raises, which is the answer to your 23 August note; Legs B has a smith squat behind the RDL and the RDL is 3 sets, which is what you have done on each of the last three Legs B nights that were not cut short by travel; the one full Legs B in that stretch, 5 September, had four. One thing is yours to answer, not mine: Legs B is now 24 sets and you have finished a Legs B in full once in eight tries (the last eight were 23, 23, 20, 18, 22, 21, 13 and 21 sets). The squat sits second so it will get done; if the night runs short it is the hanging leg raise and cable crunch at the end that fall off, and that is abs work the week then loses. If 24 is too many, say so in a note and the deload on 26 October re-sizes the day. Sets per day: Push A 22, Pull A 19, Legs A 20, Push B 24, Pull B 20, Legs B 24. Everything else holds to the end of this block on 25 October; the deload week after it is where chest, hamstrings and glutes get re-sized once there are two more weeks on the same machines.

Tonight's Pull B, for the record: the smith row at 65 kg went 9 and 9, so it holds until both top sets reach 10; straight-arm pulldown 77, 99, 110 for 12 and reverse curl 77, 88, 99 for 15, 13, 12 both hit the top of their ranges, so next Pull B starts at 110 and 99. The deadlift rows on 8 October were typed within 17 seconds, so they are recalled numbers; the deadlift holds at 225 next Pull A until 5 lands on every set. One more thing: no bodyweight has been logged since 23 August (207 lb), and the assessment week starts 2 November. A reading this week gives the review something to work with.

flags.note: Tomorrow 14 October is Legs A, not Legs B: it was due on 10 October and was not trained, and there has been no direct quad work since 28 September.
Program v2 (written today) stands: Push A swaps the rope pushdown for a lateral raise; Push B goes to 3 sets of dips and 3 of lateral raises; Legs B gains a smith squat and the RDL goes to 3 sets.
No bodyweight logged since 23 August (207 lb); the assessment week starts 2 November.

block.why: Week 3 of 4 of the third build block. The block ends 25 October; the deload runs 26 October to 1 November, the assessment week 2 to 8 November, and the prep block starts 9 November, 112 days before the show; today is 139 days out. This is the automatic run, reading the same log the review written earlier tonight read: the last session logged is Pull B at Chennai on 13 October (18 of 20 sets, face pulls skipped) and nothing has been logged since, so every verdict below was re-checked against the raw rows of 8, 12 and 13 October and repeats where the evidence is identical. Program v2, written today, stands: Push A gained a lateral raise in place of the rope pushdown, Push B went to 3 sets of dips and 3 of lateral raises, Legs B gained a smith squat and its RDL went to 3 sets. Walking any of that back tonight would need a session logged after it, and there is none. Where the block stands: three gyms in three weeks (Warsaw, Singapore, Chennai), so most lifts are re-finding a machine rather than adding weight, and the real progress is attendance (26 of 26 sets on 12 October, 18 of 20 on 13 October) and the two structural fixes (side delts and quads). Next boundary is the 26 October deload. Ten muscles sit above their ceiling on paper (chest 19, front delts 18.5, rear delts 15.5, upper back 18, biceps 18, triceps 21, forearms 11, hamstrings 18.5, glutes 18.5, adductors 8) because the count credits every helper muscle at half a set, while the targets were written as direct-set ranges; none of them is cut tonight on that arithmetic alone, and the deload is where each is re-sized, and the targets re-read in the same convention, with two more weeks on one gym's machines. Each is listed in deferred[] with that date. Two things to carry: Legs A was due on 10 October and was not trained, so tomorrow 14 October is Legs A, not Legs B; and no bodyweight has been logged since 23 August (207 lb), 51 days, with the assessment three weeks out. One question is handed to him rather than decided: Legs B is now 24 sets and he has finished a Legs B in full once in eight tries; see the brief.

chest.why: Nineteen a week on paper after the dips cut, one over the ceiling, but that counts the dips and both crossovers; the direct pressing is incline 4, chest press 3 and 3. Push days have been done in full at Chennai and Singapore (26 of 26 on 12 October, 21 of 21 on 6 October). Hold through the block; re-size at the 26 October deload with two more push weeks on the same machines.

front-delts.why: Direct front-delt work by the program's own tags is 11 sets (incline press 4, which the catalogue counts as a primary mover, shoulder press 3 on Push A and 4 on Push B), one over the ceiling of 10; the 18.5 on paper adds half credit from the chest press, crossovers and dips. Not cut tonight: the pressing is doing its job (seated press at Chennai on 12 October 18 kg for 10 then 22.5 kg for 10, 10, 10; 20 kg for 8, 8, 8 at Singapore on 6 October under that day's 10-to-12 ask) and the incline press is a chest lift first. Re-sized at the 26 October deload with the other over-ceiling muscles.

side-delts.why: Since the cable raise came off Push A on 14 September the only side-delt work in the week was the four sets of dumbbell raise on Push B: 7.5 planned against a floor of 8, 4.1 done on average. Today Push A gets a lateral raise (3 sets) in place of the rope pushdown and Push B goes from 4 sets to 3, answering his 23 August note that four in one session was a lot for a small muscle: six direct sets across two days, 9.5 a week with the press helpers.

rear-delts.why: Ten direct sets a week (reverse pec deck 3 and 3, face pulls 2 and 2); the rest is helper credit from rows and pulldowns. Reverse pec deck read 50 kg for 11, 11, 11 at Chennai on 12 October and 95 lb for 12s at Singapore on 6 October; two machines, not a rise. Face pulls were the slot skipped on 13 October, last in Pull B; they stay in and they stay last.

lats.why: Wide pulldown hit 100 for 10 on all three sets at Singapore on 8 October, the top of its range; close pulldown 130 for 8s and straight-arm pulldown 110 for 12 at Chennai on 13 October. Volume is inside the target and the lifts are moving where the gym stays the same.

upper-back.why: The smith row read 65 kg for 9, 8, 7 at Singapore on 3 October and 65 kg for 9, 9 at Chennai on 13 October, which the app flags as a stall and which is really two machines; the seated row went 105, 115, 115 for 12 at Singapore on 8 October. Eighteen on paper, of which eight are direct rows. Hold and earn 10 on both top sets at 65 kg.

traps.why: Three direct shrug sets plus helpers. On 13 October the slot was done as a reverse smith shrug, 55 kg for 16, 17, 18, inside the 12-to-20 range, so the weight holds until 20 lands; it is a different movement from the dumbbell shrug the slot names and carries its own number.

lower-back.why: No direct lower-back slot and none needed: deadlift, RDL and the bent-over row load it every week, and the only note near it was "Sick today" on the deadlift of 8 October, not a back complaint.

biceps.why: Eleven direct sets (dumbbell curl 3, hammer curl 3, incline curl 2, reverse curl 3), inside the target; the eighteen counts pulldown and row helpers. Curls are progressing: reverse curl 99 for 12 on 13 October, barbell curl 65 for 8, 8, 8 on 8 October.

triceps.why: The most over-planned muscle. By the credited count (helpers at half) it was 24 a week before today and is 21 after v2, still against a ceiling of 14; by direct sets it went from 14 to 11 (overhead extension 3 and 3, dips 3, reverse-grip pushdown 2) when the rope pushdown left Push A and dips dropped to three sets. The 10 that remain over the ceiling are press helper credit (incline, chest press, shoulder press, crossovers at half each), and that is not cut tonight: the direct work is now inside the range and the presses are chest and shoulder lifts first. At Chennai on 12 October he did skullcrushers 12.5 kg for 10, 9, 9 in the overhead slot and the reverse-grip pushdown 55 kg for 11, 12. The remainder is re-read at the 26 October deload.

forearms.why: Six direct sets (reverse curl, hammer curl), the rest helpers from shrugs, curls and hanging leg raises. Reverse curl ran 77, 88, 99 for 15, 13, 12 at Chennai on 13 October. Nothing to change.

quads.why: The most under-served muscle in the program: 8.5 planned a week before today against a floor of 10, 3.4 done a week on average. No direct quad work since Legs A at Warsaw on 28 September (leg press 190 for 8, extension 150 for 12); the feet-high leg press on 5 October credits them half a set each, and that is the 1.5 in that week. Legs A was due on 10 October and was not trained (he wrote "Sick today" on 8 October and nothing was logged until 12 October). Today's v2 adds a smith squat to Legs B, taking the week to 11.5, and tomorrow 14 October is Legs A. Raise acted on today.

hamstrings.why: Sixteen direct sets a week on paper after the RDL cut (curls 3 and 3, RDL 3, deadlift 4, leg press high 3), above the ceiling, yet only 6.9 done on average, because leg days were the ones shortened or skipped (deload week, Warsaw, the missed Legs A); RDL compliance is 79 percent over its last six visits. Not cutting curls while attendance is the problem. Re-size at the 26 October deload.

glutes.why: Credited from the RDL, deadlift, feet-high leg press, split squat and now the smith squat; there is no glute isolation and 6.1 done a week on average. The number on paper is high because every hinge and squat counts; it is not a reason to cut a hinge. Re-size at the deload.

adductors.why: Four direct sets on the machine (80 for 15, 15 at Singapore on 5 October), the rest helper credit from the leg press, split squat and the new squat. Above the ceiling on paper only. Tomorrow is a different machine, so the weight is found again, not raised.

abductors.why: Four sets a week, inside the target. The stored weight has read 135 at the home gym, 110 at Warsaw and 60 at Singapore for the same 15 reps: three machines. At Chennai it is found again on the first set, not raised from Singapore's number.

calves.why: Six sets of calf press a week, 3.8 done on average because of the missed leg days. 290 went 15 then 12 and the third set dropped to 270 at Singapore on 5 October; the Chennai leg press has not been loaded yet, so the first set finds the weight.

abs.why: Cable crunch 3 and 3 plus hanging leg raise 2. Crunch went 55 for 12, 12, 12 at Singapore on 5 October; the hanging leg raise has gone 12 then 10 on both of the last two full Legs B nights. Cable crunch is the last slot on Legs A and was the one left out when the 28 September session was cut short at 34 minutes.

smith-incline-press.why: Logged as an incline barbell at Singapore on 6 October, 75 kg for 6, 6, 6 after 70 for 8, and 165 for 6 at the old gym on 19 September. Three gyms in a month; the number to beat is 75 kg for 8 on the same bar.

machine-chest-press.why: Flagged as stalled on Push A, but the three nights are three machines: 160 for 12 on 19 September, 130 for 10 at Singapore on 6 October, and a smith bench at Chennai 75 kg for 8, 8 on 12 October. Hold and progress on whichever machine he sees twice.

cable-crossover-low-high.why: 10 for 15, 15, 15 at Singapore on 6 October, the top of the range on a stack that reads lower than the old gym (15 to 17.5 there). Next time on that stack it goes up a plate; at Chennai, find the weight on the first set.

db-shoulder-press.why: Push B at Chennai on 12 October, done as a seated dumbbell press: 18 kg for 10 to warm up, then 22.5 kg for 10, 10, 10, the top of the 8-to-10 range on all three working sets, so 25 kg next Push B. Push A is a different ask (10 to 12): 20 kg went 8, 8, 8 at Singapore on 6 October, under the floor, so Push A holds 20 kg and earns 10.

reverse-pec-deck.why: 50 kg for 11, 11, 11 at Chennai on 12 October; 95 lb for 12s at Singapore on 6 October. Two machines, so neither is a rise over the other. Earn 12 on all three at 50 kg, then up.

overhead-cable-triceps.why: Done as skullcrushers 12.5 kg for 10, 9, 9 at Chennai on 12 October; no note says why the slot was swapped, so nothing is assumed about that gym's cables (cable crossovers and a cable pushdown were logged there the same night). At Singapore on 6 October it was 100, 115, 110 for 12. Same slot on both push days is deliberate; the triceps cut came from the pushdown and the dips, not here. Hold: on a new movement the first visit sets the number.

rope-pushdown.why: Leaves Push A today for a lateral raise: it was the third triceps slot on a day whose triceps are already over the ceiling, and the week had no side-delt work outside Push B. 90 for 11, 12 at Singapore on 6 October was fine work; it is the balance that was wrong.

machine-lateral-raise.why: New today on Push A, 3 sets of 12 to 15, after the shoulder press. No lateral raise machine has been logged at any gym yet; if there is none, do the cable or dumbbell raise in this slot and mark it on the card. Start light and find the weight on the first set; the dumbbell raise on Push B is at 7.5 kg for 10s.

deadlift.why: 265 for 5 in August, 255 for 4 and 3 in September ("Too early in morning"), 225 for 6, 4, 4, 4 at Singapore on 8 October with "Sick today." Those four rows were entered within 17 seconds of each other, so they were typed after the fact, not timed; a recalled set is not a number to progress from. Flagged as stalled and it is. Hold 225 next Pull A and ask for 5 on every set before it moves; if that fails twice more, the deload is where it rotates to a rack pull or a trap-bar pull.

lat-pulldown-wide.why: 100 for 10, 10, 10 at Singapore on 8 October, top of the range on that stack. Up one plate next time on the same stack.

seated-cable-row-wide.why: 105, 115, 115 for 12s at Singapore on 8 October (three sets of the four asked). Top of the range: 120 next time, and all four sets.

db-curl.why: Done as a barbell curl at Singapore, 65 for 8, 8, 8 on 8 October, the bottom of the range. Hold 65 and earn 10.

cable-hammer-curl.why: On 8 October at Singapore all three sets hit 12 (35, 35, 36), the top of the range, which is the program's rule for a raise: 40 next Pull A on that stack. The two nights before were not there yet (36 for 12, 12 then 35 for 11 on 20 September; 35 for 11, 11, 10 on 10 September, at the old gym).

face-pulls.why: 15 then 20 for 15 at Singapore on 8 October; skipped on 13 October at Chennai, the last slot of a 70-minute Pull B. It stays in and it stays last: two sets, two minutes, and they count toward the rear-delt week. Hold 20.

leg-press-low.why: Flagged as stalled: 240 for 8 at the home gym in August, 180 and 160 in September, then this lift's own last reading, 150, 170, 190 for 8, 8, 8 at Warsaw on 28 September. Four gyms. Not trained since; Legs A was due on 10 October and missed. The feet-high press at Singapore on 5 October ran the same three numbers for 10. Tomorrow at Chennai, a machine never loaded, runs that ramp again at 8 to 10 reps, and the second visit sets the real level.

db-bulgarian-split-squat.why: 17.5 for 10, 10 on 28 September, the top of the range, after 17.5 for 10 on 13 September. Dumbbells are dumbbells in any gym: up to 20 tomorrow (9 or 10 kg).

leg-curl.why: 120 for 10, 10, 11 at Singapore on 5 October; 145 for 12 at Warsaw on 28 September. Different machines. At Chennai, start at 120 and aim for 12 on every set.

leg-extension.why: Flagged as stalled at 150 for 12 to 14 since July at the old gym, 150 for 12 at Warsaw on 28 September. Not seen at Singapore or Chennai yet. Tomorrow is a first guess at Chennai; the stall is a gym-change artefact until two nights on one machine say otherwise.

hip-adductor.why: 80 for 15, 15 at Singapore on 5 October, 110 for 15 at Warsaw, 105 at the home gym: the number belongs to the machine. Tomorrow at Chennai the first set is at 80 to find the weight and the second goes to 90 if 15 was easy; a raise is earned on the second visit to the same machine.

hip-abductor.why: 60 for 15, 15 at Singapore on 5 October; 110 for 15, 15 at Warsaw on 28 September; 135 for 13, 13 at the home gym on 20 August and 135 for 15 there on 5 September: three machines. Tomorrow at Chennai the first set is at 60 to find the weight and the second goes to 70 if 15 was easy.

standing-calf-raise.why: 290 for 15, then 290 for 12, then a drop to 270 for 14 at Singapore on 5 October; 280 for 12s at Warsaw on 28 September. The Chennai leg press has not been loaded yet: first set 270 to find it, then 290 for 12s, the weight Singapore's first two sets carried.

cable-crunch.why: 55 for 12, 12, 12 at Singapore on 5 October, top of the range on that stack. At Chennai: first set 55 to find the stack, then 60 for 10s if it was easy.

hanging-leg-raise.why: 12 and 12 on 16 August and 5 September, then 12 then 10 on 17 September and 12 then 10 on 5 October: the second set has slipped to 10 on the last two full Legs B nights, so the trend is regressing, not holding. Bodyweight, so the ask stays 12 and 12; it moves to a weighted or slower version at the deload if the second set is still at 10 by then (dated in deferred[]).

assisted-dips.why: Bench dips 17, 17, 17, 17 at Chennai on 12 October (the 30 September "Dips" at Warsaw were a different movement, not compared). Sets go 4 to 3 today for the day's and the triceps' total; the reps keep climbing toward 20.

db-lateral-raise.why: 10 lb for 15 to warm up, then 7.5 kg for 10, 10, 10 at Chennai on 12 October, under the 12-rep floor; 7 kg for 15s at Warsaw. Sets go 4 to 3 today (his 23 August note; Push A now carries three of its own). Hold 7.5 kg and earn 12.

cable-crossover-high-low.why: 35 kg for 15 then 45 kg for 15 and 14 at Chennai on 12 October, on a stack that reads nothing like the old gym (27 there). One of the two sets at 45 was under 15, so the plate is not earned yet: hold 45 and get 15 on both.

reverse-grip-pushdown.why: 55 kg for 11, 12 at Chennai on 12 October. Up one plate when 12 lands on both sets.

smith-bent-over-row.why: 65 kg for 9, 9 at Chennai on 13 October (after 55 kg for 10 and 60 kg for 10); 65 kg for 9, 8, 7 at Singapore on 3 October; 155 for 8s at the old gym on 15 September. The flag is right that the top number has not moved on two visits, but they were two machines, and Chennai held 9 on both top sets where Singapore fell to 7. Hold 65 kg and earn 10 on both top sets.

lat-pulldown-close.why: 115 then 130 for 8, 8 at Chennai on 13 October, the bottom of the range. Hold 130 and earn 10.

straight-arm-pulldown.why: 77, 99, 110 for 12s at Chennai on 13 October, top of the range. Next Pull B at Chennai starts at 110 and the top set goes up.

db-shrug.why: Done as a reverse smith shrug at Chennai on 13 October, 55 kg for 16, 17, 18, inside the 12-to-20 range that was opened on 27 September so that reps, not weight, would climb. Hold 55 kg until 20 lands on all three sets. It is a different movement from the dumbbell shrug the slot names and carries its own number.

incline-db-curl.why: 25 for 10 then 30 for 9 at Chennai on 13 October. Hold 30 and earn 10 on both sets.

cable-reverse-curl.why: 77, 88, 99 for 15, 13, 12 at Chennai on 13 October, top of the range on every set. Start at 99 next time.

smith-rdl.why: 155, 175, 185 for 8 at Singapore on 5 October (one working set at 185 after two ramp sets), 135, 165, 185 for 8 on 17 September, 205 for 9 in August; three sets done on each of the last three full nights against four asked. Flagged as stalled. Sets go 4 to 3 today to match what happens; the ramp gets shorter so two of the three are at 185, and the weight moves when 185 goes 10 on both.

smith-squat.why: New today on Legs B, 3 sets of 8 to 10 behind the RDL. Start around 60 kg on the bar and find the working weight on the second set. At a gym with no smith machine, a barbell back squat or a goblet squat in the slot is the same work; mark it on the card.

leg-press-high.why: 150, 170, 190 for 10s at Singapore on 5 October, from 170 for 10 in September. Earn 12 at 190 and then 200.

changes_today.why: This puts side-delt work back on Push A, which has had none since the cable lateral raise came off on 14 September. That removal gave two reasons: the weight had sat at 10 lb on the old gym's stack since August, and Push B already carried three dumbbell lateral raises, the lift he had asked about on 23 August. Both are answered differently now: this is a new slot on new machines, not the stuck 10 lb, and Push B goes from four sets to three in the same version, so the week is six direct side-delt sets across two days instead of four in one. Side delts were planned at 7.5 sets a week against a floor of 8 and averaged 4.1 done. Triceps were planned at 24 a week against a ceiling of 14, with the overhead extension already on both push days, so the rope pushdown, Push A's third triceps slot, is the one that gives way. No lateral raise machine has been logged at any gym yet; where there is none, a cable or dumbbell raise in this slot is the same work. Mark it as "doing something else" on the card.
The lateral raise goes straight after the shoulder press, while the shoulders are warm and before the rear-delt and triceps work, instead of last in the session where the slot it replaced used to be.

Push B was 26 sets, the heaviest day in the program, after three separate raises in September that nobody added up, and triceps are the most over-planned muscle in the week (24 sets against a ceiling of 14, with the overhead extension on both push days and a pushdown on this one). This walks back the 22 September raise from 3 to 4 after one session at four: bench dips went 17, 17, 17, 17 at Chennai on 12 October, which shows there is plenty left in him, and that is exactly why three hard sets at 12 to 20 reps, with the reps climbing toward 20, is enough stimulus for this slot on this day. (The 30 September "Dips" at Warsaw and the 12 October "Bench dips" are different movements; the reps comparison between them is not made.)

On 23 August he wrote that four sets of lateral raises seemed a lot for such a small muscle; the program cut it to three on 28 August and put it back to four on 21 September because it was the only side-delt work in the week. Now that Push A carries three sets of its own, Push B goes back to three: six sets across two days instead of four in one. On 12 October the four sets were a 10 lb warm-up for 15 and then 7.5 kg for 10, 10, 10, under the 12-rep floor.

The program asks four sets and he has done three on each of the last three Legs B nights that were not cut short by travel: 155, 185, 205 for 8, 9, 9 on 16 August (18 sets that night), 135, 165, 185 for 8 on 17 September (21 sets in 23 minutes) and 155, 175, 185 for 8 at Singapore on 5 October (21 of 22 sets); Warsaw on 24 September was two sets. The one night in that window with all four, 5 September, was also the only full Legs B (22 of 22) and the best recent work on this lift: 135 for 8, 155 for 10, 180 for 10, 180 for 10. So four sets happen when the night is full, which has been once in eight tries. Three sets, with the ramp kept short so two of them are working sets, is what he actually does; prescribing a fourth that usually does not happen makes the card wrong most nights. It also keeps Legs B at 24 sets with the squat added instead of 25.

Quads are the most under-served muscle in the program: planned 8.5 sets a week against a floor of 10, averaging 3.4 done over four weeks, and zero this week because Legs A was due on 10 October and not trained. The only knee-dominant compound work in the week is the two leg presses plus the single-leg split squat; there is no two-legged squat with a bar. Legs B has no quad-first lift at all (the feet-high leg press is a glute and hamstring press). A smith squat goes second, behind the RDL, while he is fresh. Chennai, where he is now, has a smith machine (the row was done on it on 13 October); at a gym without one, a barbell back squat or a goblet squat in this slot is the same work, marked on the card. Legs B goes from 22 to 24 sets with the RDL at three; the day stays under its cap and the week moves by one set.

findings.finding: The RDL cut (4 to 3) rested on "three on each of the last three full Legs B nights", but none of those nights was full, and the one full Legs B in the window, 5 September (22 of 22), had four RDL sets (135×8, 155×10, 180×10, 180×10), the best recent work on the lift, omitted from the change.
findings.why: The v2 change entry (program.json and changes_today) now quotes all five nights correctly: three sets on 16 August, 17 September and 5 October, two at Warsaw, four on 5 September, and says four sets happen when the night is full, which has been once in eight tries. The decision stands on that corrected basis; the brief says the same.

findings.finding: Set creep on the day the packet cuts for non-completion: Legs B goes 22 to 24 by adding a 3-set compound with 180 s rest to a day he has finished in full once in eight tries (23, 23, 20, 18, 22, 21, 13, 21 sets), while the RDL is cut because a fourth set "never happens".
